Research Papers:
Riess et al. (2021), "A Comprehensive Measurement of the Local Value of the Hubble
Constant with 1% Precision Using HST and Gaia EDR3." This paper from the SH0ES
collaboration provided the local H₀ measurement of 73.0 ± 1.0 km/s/Mpc, highlighting the
Hubble tension that FSUFT 4.2 seeks to resolve.
Planck Collaboration (2020), "Planck 2018 Results. VI. Cosmological Parameters." This
seminal paper gave the CMB-based H₀ value of 67.4 ± 0.5 km/s/Mpc, along with parameters
like S₈ = 0.832 ± 0.013 and N_eff = 3.046, which I used as benchmarks for FSUFT’s
predictions.
Bulbul et al. (2014), "Detection of an Unidentified Emission Line in the Stacked X-ray
Spectrum of Galaxy Clusters." This paper identified the 3.5 keV line in the Perseus cluster
(flux ~ 5–10 × 10⁻⁶ photons/cm²/s), which inspired FSUFT’s sterile neutrino (SNS)
mechanism.
Boyarsky et al. (2014), "An Unidentified Line in X-ray Spectra of the Andromeda Galaxy and
Perseus Cluster." This corroborated the 3.5 keV line, reinforcing the need for new physics
beyond ΛCDM.
Hu et al. (2000), "Fuzzy Cold Dark Matter: The Wave Properties of Ultralight Particles." This
introduced the concept of fuzzy dark matter (m ~ 10⁻²² eV), which I adapted for FSUFT’s
scalar bosons (SBs) to explain dwarf galaxy core softening.
Navarro, Frenk, and White (1996), "The Structure of Cold Dark Matter Halos." This paper
defined the NFW profile (ρ ∝  r⁻¹), which predicts cuspy galaxy cores that FSUFT’s fuzzy
dark matter counters with cored profiles (rc = 0.47 kpc).
Books and General References:
Cosmology by Steven Weinberg (2008). This book provided a comprehensive foundation in
modern cosmology, including the FLRW metric and ΛCDM framework, which I used to build
FSUFT’s fluid modifications.
Introduction to Cosmology by Barbara Ryden (2016). This accessible text helped me
understand the basics of cosmic expansion, the CMB, and structure formation, which I
translated into FSUFT’s layman’s sections.
The Inflationary Universe by Alan Guth (1997). Guth’s work on inflation inspired FSUFT’s
primordial scalar axions (PSAs) and the tensor-to-scalar ratio (r = 0.0079 ± 0.0005),
connecting early universe dynamics to our fluid model.
Gravitation by Misner, Thorne, and Wheeler (1973). This classic text on general relativity
informed my understanding of space-time dynamics, which I extended into a fluid paradigm
with gravity leakage via KKGs.
